content: task-add-trail-link-path-script closed. The link-path script (Test-TrailLink.ps1) turned out to already exist from commit 660b993, predating this session -- the queue items open status was simply stale bookkeeping. Discovered this only after my first attempt silently clobbered the existing file (explicit mode:rewrite bypassed the write tools own collision guard); restored it via git checkout and diffed against my draft instead of assuming my version was needed. That restore-and-compare turned up a real, previously-unverified bug: the original script hard-required -TrailId even when -TrailPath was supplied directly, contradicting its own docstring and every sibling phase scripts convention -- so there was genuine, non-redundant work after all, just much smaller than a full rewrite. Applied a minimal patch (merged precondition checks, added task_id to the output for parity with New-Trail.ps1), verified all 5 documented paths against real fixtures, updated the stale queue item with a resolution note, committed (d47f743) and pushed. Lesson worth carrying forward: check git log / existing files before writing a new script for a queue item marked open -- open does not reliably mean unstarted in this repo, and the write tools collision guard is bypassable by an explicit mode, so it is not a substitute for checking first.
